info.title: Void by A-to-Mind
info.summary: Void's public API: code review, Void as an MCP server, and the list of what Void can do.
info.description: Void (https://a-to-mind.com) is a blank stage where anything someone asks for appears. Everything a person sees runs in the browser; open https://a-to-mind.com/?q={ask} to run any ask in plain words. The operations below are the ones meant for other programs. Every other /api route is Void's own (the page, the owner, signed-in accounts) and is left out on purpose. Calls from other websites' pages are refused (no CORS): call from a server, a CLI or an agent. Each connection gets 60 requests a minute per route.

get.summary: Scores, standings, game detail and team schedules for 12 leagues (free, read only)
get.description: Free and read only, no key, no premium tier. A league from a closed list (epl, laliga, bundesliga, seriea, ligue1, mls, ucl, nba, nfl, mlb, nhl, f1) and a day return that day's games (live, final or upcoming) as one shape; view=standings returns the tables, view=game the events, team stats, line-ups, box score and play by play, view=team a team's next and last games, view=form each team's last five results and a Verse rating. The data comes from ESPN's unofficial public site API (OpenLigaDB behind it for the Bundesliga, Jolpica for F1) and may be delayed by a minute or more; answers are edge-cached from 20 seconds while a game is live to six hours once final, and a source that fails gives the last good copy marked stale. Call it from a server or an agent (no CORS). Scores are public facts shown for reading: no odds, no betting data.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: A day, YYYY-MM-DD, from 2000-01-01 to 400 days ahead; today when left out.

parameters.name: span
parameters.description: 7 for the seven days from date (scores view only).

200.description: { ok: true, league, view, date, at, source, games | groups | game, events, stats, lineups, players, plays | form, elo }; stale: true when the last good copy is served.

429.description: More than 30 uncached requests a minute from one connection.

get.summary: Your reports and the owner's answers (paying users)

post.description: Send code or a unified diff. The instant checks (bugs, security holes, risky habits, with line numbers) are free and need no key. With a Void Pro key, a Verse Code Review Pro license key, or the owner's token in Authorization, the answer also carries the closer read by an AI reviewer (`review: 'model'`), up to a daily cap. For a diff, only the added lines are reviewed and line numbers are in the new file. Code over 60,000 characters is cut there. The free GitHub Action atomeam/void-loop/review@main calls this for every pull request.

200.description: The findings. Without a key `tier` is `free`, `review` is `rules` and `upgrade` says how to get the closer read. A `note` says why the closer read did not run when a key was sent (today's cap used, the model off or busy).

findings.message: a key, token or password is written into the code. Anyone who sees the code (or the repo history) has it. Move it to an environment variable or a secret store, and change the key if this code was ever shared.
putting a variable into innerHTML lets any HTML in it run (a script tag, an onerror handler): an XSS hole if the text can come from a user. Use textContent, or escape the text first.

example.upgrade: Verse Code Review Pro adds a closer read by an AI reviewer: https://a-to-mind.com/code-review/

401.description: The Authorization header carries a review key or license key Void does not know.

post.description: Void's MCP server: the streamable HTTP transport, answered as plain JSON (no event stream). Methods: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`. The tools are read-only: `review_code` (the instant checks), `review_code_closer` (the closer read; send the same Authorization header /api/review takes), `moon_phase`, `meteor_showers`, a `skill_<name>` tool for each of Void's ten proven read-only skills with the most evidence (answered the way `ask_void` is, with a link to the skill itself) `seo_audit`, `readability` and `colour_contrast` (the SEO audit, readability and WCAG contrast tools Verse runs on its own pages) and `skill_health` (the skill-family health metrics from /skills/families.json). A JSON-RPC notification (no `id`) gets 202 with no body. Unparseable JSON still gets 200 with JSON-RPC error -32700. GET answers 405.

200.description: The JSON-RPC reply (a result, or an error object).

202.description: A notification was received; there is no reply.

get.description: The static MCP Server Card (SEP-2127, schema v1) at the reserved place beside the endpoint: Verse's name, version, repository, icon and the streamable HTTP endpoint with the protocol version it speaks. It lists no tools; an MCP client lists them with `tools/list`. Public and read-only.

get.summary: Everything Void can do, with asks to try
get.description: Built live from Void's skills, so it never drifts. Each tool is used by opening https://a-to-mind.com/?q={ask} in a browser; `mcp` describes the MCP endpoint and its tools. This is the one response other websites may read (CORS open).

get.summary: How far each skill is checked: proven, checked, tested or experiment
get.description: Every skill Void has, in its family, with a rating earned from evidence only: its own tests, the browser suite, and real asks in the everyday benchmark (proven: all three, or two with 3+ real asks; checked: two; tested: one; experiment: none). `failing` lists the benchmark asks a skill got wrong on the last clean run on main, when there are any. Generated by tools/families.mjs and served as a static file. Void asked for it (2026-10-13): "a machine-readable 'skill-health' endpoint that returns the 'proven' vs 'tested' status for each skill".

200.description: The families and each skill's rating.

families.name: Making things
families.for: figures, 3D models, prints, drawings and parts

skills.name: forge
skills.why: a self-test, 10 real asks in the benchmark

get.summary: What A-to-Mind sells, with live prices
get.description: Read from the Gumroad store and refreshed when older than six hours. A product that is no longer sold stays listed with `available: false`.

200.description: The products. `source` is `store` (saved catalog), `live` (read straight from Gumroad) or `none`.

reviewKey.description: Optional. A Verse Pro review key (`vr1.…`, made by a signed-in paid account on a-to-mind.com) or a Verse Code Review Pro license key. It unlocks the closer read; without it the instant checks run free.

BadRequest.description: The body is not JSON, or it has no `code` or `diff` of at least 8 characters.

CrossSite.description: The request came from another website's page. Call from a server, a CLI or an agent instead.

TooBig.description: The body is over the route's size cap (70,000 bytes for /api/review, 64,000 for /api/mcp).

SlowDown.description: Over 60 requests a minute from this connection on this route, or too many wrong keys. Wait for `retry-after` seconds.

diff.description: A unified diff; its added lines are reviewed.

lang.description: The language, when it can't be told from the code (for example javascript, python, go, dockerfile, terraform).

ask.description: What to look for, in plain words. It can also name the language ("review my python").

imports.description: For a diff: each touched file's import and top-level declaration lines, by path, so the closer read does not call a name declared outside the hunk missing.

line.description: 1-based line in the code (in the new file, for a diff).

kind.description: What sort of finding it is, for example `bug` or `risk`.

rule.description: The check that found it, for example `hardcoded-secret`.

message.description: What is wrong and how to fix it, in plain words.

lang.description: The language Void read the code as.

ms.description: How long the instant checks took.

answer.description: The closer read, when it ran.

quoted.description: How the closer read's findings were checked against the code: kept, dropped, whether the model's JSON parsed, echoes and refuted claims.

left.description: Closer reads left today for this key.

note.description: Why the closer read did not run, when a key was sent.

upgrade.description: How to get the closer read (free tier only).

id.description: Leave it out for a notification.

why.description: The evidence behind the rating, in words.

failing.description: Benchmark asks this skill got wrong on the last clean run on main (up to 3).

description.description: The product's own description, up to 800 characters.

refreshed.description: When the saved catalog was last read from the store.
